caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 135 of 2009
lawyer:
Md. Zahirul Islam, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
For the Respondent ------ Not represented
parties:
Soharaf Uddin @ Shohrab ------ Petitioner
Vs.
The State ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J. This criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 26.11.2008 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 17849 of 2011 discharging the Rule and thereby affirming the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 29.01.2004 passed by the learned Special Judge, Special Tribunal No. 6, Kishoregonj in Special Tribunal Case No. 02 of 2002 convicting the petitioner under section 19A of the Arms Act and sentencing him thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 10 (ten) years. 

 2. The facts, leading to the filing of the examined by the defence. petition for leave to appeal, in short, arc that the informant, Sub-Inspector of  police, Abdul Awal lodged an First Information Report with the Officer-in-Charge, Kishoregonj Police Station Case No. 01 dated 20.08.2001 corresponding to G.R. No. 395(2)2001. The prosecution case, in short, is that the informant with forces arrested accused-petitioner; Soharaf Uddin @ Soharab on 01.08.2001 in connection with Kishoregonj P.S. Case No. 06 dated 08.12.2000 under sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code. During interrogation, the petitioner admitted that he has a pipe gun and some looted articles with him. According to the admission of the petitioner, the informant party went to his house on 02.08.2001 at night about 02:35 hours and recovered a pipe gun from the house of the petitioner and prepared seizure list. The petitioner could not show any document about the arms. Consequently, the above mentioned case was initiated. 

 4. After that, the case was sent to the Court of the learned Special Judge, Special Tribunal No.  1, Kishoregonj and numbered as Special Tribunal Case No.  02 of 2002 and subsequently, the case was transferred to Special Tribunal No.  6 for trial. 

 7. The defence case as could be gathered from the trend of cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses is of total denial contending, inter-alia, that the arms was not recovered from control and possession of the petitioner, who has been falsely implicated in this case. His further defence is that the petitioner was kept in the police custody for about three hours and in the Meantime, the persons inimical to him kept the arms in his house for implicating him in this case and the alleged confessional statement is not true and voluntary, inasmuch as, the same is the product of physical/mental torture. 

 8. After close of the prosecution case, the accused in dock, was examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, to which, he pleaded not guilty and repeated his innocence the defence did not however examine any witness. 

 10. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the Special Tribunal, the petitioner preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.  3472 of 2006 before the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the aforesaid judgment and order passed by the Special Tribunal and obtained Rule. 

 13. Mr.  Md. Zahirul Islam, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing on behalf of the leave petitioner, submits that the prosecution failed to prove that the country made pipe gun was recovered from the active control and possession of the leave petitioner and that the High Court Division without taking into consideration this broad fact discharged the Rule. He further submits that the seizure list witnesses, who are the only local witnesses in whose presence the country made pipe gun was recovered did not support the prosecution case of recovery of country made pipe gun from the possession of the leave petitioner and that virtually there was no legal evidence warranting conviction of the leave petitioner and the High Court Division without taking into consideration these aspects of the case discharged the Rule. 

 14. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate, the impugned judgment and the materials on record. The High Court Division found that P.Ws. 4-8 deposed that on the night following 02.08.2001 at about 2.30 a.m. they searched the house of the accused-petitioner Soharab Uddin and seized one country made pipe gun from within a carton of biscuit and seized the pipe gun by preparing a seizure list. The High Court Division further found that P.W.4 proved the seizure list and his signature thereon. He also identified the country made pipe gun marked as material exhibit-1. Taking into consideration, the evidence of P.W. 1 Sekender and P.W. 2 Abdur Roaf, the local witnesses in whose presence the country made pipe gun was recovered, the High Court Division found that both of them proved the seizure list marked as exhibit-1 and P.Ws.1 and 2 also identified their signatures on the seizure list marked as exhibit-1(ka) and 2 (kha) respectively. The High Court Division, however, noticed that both P.Ws.1 and 2 indirectly wanted to say that they did not see the actual occurrence of seizure of country made pipe gun from the house of the petitioner but that both of them proved the seizure list and admitted their respective signatures on it, which proved recovery of arms from the house of the accused. The High Court Division also noted that P.Ws.1 and 2 did not have the courage to tell the whole truth but that they admitted putting signatures on the seizure list, which indirectly proved the genuineness of the case.
